newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WOMAN RAPED ON S.AFRICA'S JAIL ISLAND.
newsitem.headline: WOMAN RAPED ON S.AFRICA'S JAIL ISLAND.

text.p: A black woman member of South Africa's ruling African National Congress has been raped on the former penal colony of Robben Island by a white man with a political grudge, ANC Women's League leaders said on Wednesday.
They told a news conference there were just 21 men on the island at the time of the rape on Monday night but that 48 hours later police had failed to arrest anyone.
"We think it's absolutely unsatisfactory," said ANC member of parliament Baleka Kgositsile. "We smell a cover-up."

The rape victim, Nombiso Gasa, was a curator at the anti- apartheid museum into which the island jail, where President Nelson Mandela spent 18 years of his jail term for treason, has been transformed.

Kgositsile quoted her as saying a white man with a heavy Afrikaans accent had burst into her room with a gun and told her no one would hear her scream, adding: "You are one of these who wants to change the island."
"So clearly this is a person who comes from the old establishment," Kgositsile said.
Several prison service officers are still on the island.
The last common law prisoners left the jail in December and on January 1 it was formally declared a state-run museum.
"The symbolism of this having happened on Robben Island does not escape us," Women's League spokeswoman Lindi Sisulu said.
"Robben Island for most of us represents that which we would have wanted to forget about, the oppression in this country.
"For this to happen is a slap in the face for reconciliation, it's a slap in the face for women despite all that we've had to endure," she told the news conference.
Kgositsile said Minister of Safety and Security Sydney Mufamadi had taken a personal interest in the case.
The victim had asked to be publicly identified, despite local laws which bar publication of the names of rape victims.
Police had no immediate comment on the allegations of a cover-up. They said the rape had happened in the dark and the victim had not been able to identify her assailant.
